learning_outcomes.text: Have profound knowledge of basic principles of heat transfer and engineering thermodynamics.
Have knowledge and understanding of numerical manipulations and orders of magnitude of various parameters.
Understand and explain the physical mechanisms.
Understand new situations and problems by developing his own equations.
Demonstrate skill in the use of empirical and practical correlations and ability to calculate heat and work exchanged in thermal machine components.
Demonstrate capacity for reading and understand other texts on related topics.

syllabus_topics: Heat diffusion: rectangular and cylindrical bodies, homogeneous and multi-layers, steady state and lumped transient models
Heat convection: boundary layer on a flat plate (laminar and turbulent), thermal boundary layer, empirical and practical correlations for forced and natural convection
Heat radiation: electromagnetic spectrum, thermal radiation, emissive power, radiation properties, Kirchhoff law, black and gray bodies, shape factors, radiation network
The first law for closed and open systems
The second law for closed and open systems

assessment_methods.method: Written exam (3 questions: 2 on heat transfer, 1 on engineering thermodynamics)

assessment_rules: The exam is only written and consists of 3 questions concerning the main topics discussed in the course to be solved within 3 hours. The final score is determined by giving the same weight to the three questions. An optional possibility to split the written test into two parts is provided, for example, the first part related to heat transfer, and the second related to engineering thermodynamics.
bibliography: Y. A. Cengel and A. Ghajar. Heat and Mass Transfer, 6th Edition, McGraw Hill, 2020.
Y. A. Cengel and M. Boles. Thermodynamics: An Engineering Approach, 9th Edition, McGraw-Hill, 2019.
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Industriale (Industrial Engineering), classe L-9 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria industriale
